questions.prompt: In AIDS, why do patients suffer from many different infections rather than just HIV?

options.text: HIV changes all of the patient's antibodies into IgE that cause allergies
Losing helper T cells weakens B cell activation and immune coordination
HIV infects every type of white blood cell equally and destroys them
HIV destroys MHC-1 on all body cells, so NK cells attack everything

questions.explanation: Helper T cells are central coordinators.

why.A: HIV doesn't convert antibodies to IgE.

questions.prompt: Which feature keeps a cytotoxic T cell from killing a B cell that is presenting a bacterial antigen?

options.text: B cells release perforin inhibitors to protect themselves
B cells carry no antigens on their surface at any time
The B cell displays it on MHC-2, which CD8 can't bind
Cytotoxic T cells can't enter the lymph nodes where B cells live

questions.explanation: When this system fails, autoimmune disease can result.

why.A: B cells don't release perforin inhibitors.
why.D: Cytotoxic T cells reach lymph nodes.

options.text: Helper T cells kill infected cells with perforin.
Helper T cells release interleukins.
Cytotoxic T cells kill infected cells with perforin and granzyme.
Antigen-presenting cells use MHC-2.
NK cells also use perforin and granzymes.

questions.explanation: Helper T cells help; cytotoxic T cells and NK cells kill.

why.B: True — helper T cells release interleukins.
why.C: True — cytotoxic T cells use perforin and granzyme.
why.E: True — NK cells use perforin and granzymes.

questions.prompt: Which cell types can kill a virus-infected body cell, and what does each detect?

options.text: Mast cells (by binding IgE) and B cells (by displaying antigen on MHC-2)
Neutrophils (by reading MHC-1) and eosinophils (by binding CD4 on the cell)
Helper T cells (antigen on MHC-2) and plasma cells (by secreting antibodies)
Cytotoxic T cells (antigen on MHC-1) and NK cells (missing MHC-1 or antibodies)

why.A: Mast and B cells don't kill infected cells.
why.B: Neutrophils and eosinophils don't read MHC this way.
why.C: Helper T and plasma cells don't kill.

questions.prompt: A virus evolves to stop its host cell from displaying viral antigens on MHC-1 by removing MHC-1 entirely. What defense would still catch it?

options.text: NK cells, which attack cells lacking MHC-1
Cytotoxic T cells, which read antigen on MHC-1
Helper T cells, which read antigen on MHC-2
IgA antibodies neutralizing it inside the cell

questions.explanation: The two systems cover each other's gaps.

questions.prompt: Which Module 22 idea and Module 23 idea are linked by the Fc receptor?

options.text: IgM pentamers and the perforin that cytotoxic T cells release
Burnet's clonal selection and apoptosis of virus-infected body cells
Antibody variable regions and the MHC-1 display stand on body cells
Antibody constant regions and NK/eosinophil antibody-dependent cytotoxicity

questions.explanation: Fc receptors bind the constant region.

why.A: IgM and perforin aren't linked by Fc.
why.B: Clonal selection isn't an Fc idea.
why.C: Variable regions bind antigen, not Fc.

questions.prompt: A cancer drug made from monoclonal antibodies carries chemotherapy straight to tumor cells. Why is it called a 'magic bullet'?

options.text: Its variable region binds only tumor antigens, sparing most healthy cells
It removes MHC-1 from tumor cells so that NK cells will attack them
It activates helper T cells everywhere in the body at the same time
It makes the tumor explode the moment the antibody touches it

questions.explanation: Targeted delivery reduces chemo's side effects.

why.C: It doesn't activate T cells everywhere.

questions.prompt: How do helper T cells resemble a 'second opinion' in the immune system?

options.text: They kill the antigen-presenting cell after checking what it displays
They replace the need for B cells, so no antibodies are needed at all
They confirm an APC's and a B cell's antigen is foreign before activation
They make the antibodies themselves after the B cell recognizes the antigen

why.A: Helper T cells don't kill APCs.
why.D: Helper T cells don't make antibodies.

questions.prompt: A COVID monoclonal antibody prevents infection by binding the spike protein. Which mechanism is this, and what receptor is blocked?

options.text: Antibody-dependent cytotoxicity; Fc
Agglutination; CD4
Neutralization; ACE2
Opsonization; MHC-1

questions.prompt: Necrotic tissue triggers inflammation, but cells killed by cytotoxic T cells usually don't. Why?

options.text: Cytotoxic T cells release antihistamines along with perforin
Apoptotic cells are never phagocytized, so nothing alerts mast cells
Necrosis only happens in bacteria, never in human tissue
Apoptotic cells recruit macrophages to clean up before contents spill

questions.prompt: Which test would best identify WHICH type of white blood cell is elevated?

options.text: A rapid antigen strip with a control line
A differential WBC count under the microscope
Measuring the thickness of the buffy coat
A titer graph of IgM and IgG over time

questions.explanation: The buffy coat only gives total WBCs.

why.C: The buffy coat doesn't show cell types.

questions.prompt: Why does the rapid antigen strip include chicken and rabbit antibodies that have nothing to do with COVID?

options.text: They detect a second virus, like influenza, at the same time
They form the control line, showing the sample ran up the strip
They neutralize the sample so it is safe to throw away
They amplify the COVID signal so the test line is darker

questions.explanation: Rabbit anti-chicken antibodies capture the dyed chicken antibodies.

why.D: They don't amplify the T line.

questions.prompt: Which pathway would a vaccine made of a purified viral PROTEIN most likely use to activate B cells?

options.text: T-dependent activation with APCs and helper T cells
Direct B cell activation by complement C3b alone
T-independent activation by repeating sugar units
NK cell activation through Fc receptors on the cell

questions.explanation: Slides: protein antigens need helper T cells.

why.B: C3b alone doesn't activate B cells here.
why.D: NK cells don't activate B cells.

questions.prompt: Trace what happens when a cytotoxic T cell finds a virus-infected cell, and explain why this protects the body.
questions.explanation: The infected cell displays viral antigens on MHC-1; a matching cytotoxic T cell binds with its TCR and CD8; it secretes perforin (holes) and granzyme (enters, triggers apoptosis); the cell dies tidily, with macrophages cleaning up. Killing it before it releases new viruses protects neighboring cells.

questions.prompt: Explain how a home rapid antigen test can give a positive, a negative, and an invalid result.
questions.explanation: Dyed monoclonal antibodies on the conjugate pad bind viral antigen; fixed antibodies at the T line capture the antigen–antibody complex (red line = positive). Dyed chicken antibodies are captured by rabbit anti-chicken antibodies at the C line, proving the sample migrated. T + C = positive; C only = negative; no C line (with or without T) = invalid.
